Acquisition Planning & Strategy.qtype: an acquisition-strategy question — RFO Part 7 planning built on RFO Part 10 market research: competitive posture, timing, and what the file must prove.
Acquisition Planning & Strategy.smes: the PM/requiring activity, Legal (JA), the Competition Advocate, and your pricing office.
Acquisition Planning & Strategy.rule: Strategy precedes paper: no solicitation, bridge, or J&A before the rights-deliverables-market inventory is done — and lack of advance planning never justifies skipping it (RFO Part 6).

Authority, Unauthorized Commitments & Ra.qtype: an authority question — RFO 1.402 warrant authority and the RFO 1.405 ratification lane: who can bind the Government, and what happens when someone who can't, did.
Authority, Unauthorized Commitments & Ra.smes: Legal (JA) first, your COCO/flight chief, and FM for the funds picture.
Authority, Unauthorized Commitments & Ra.rule: Only a warranted CO binds the Government (RFO 1.402). Apparent authority binds nothing — an unauthorized commitment stays unratified until an official with actual authority runs all six RFO 1.405 elements.

Procurement Integrity.qtype: a Procurement Integrity Act question — RFO 3.104: protected information and what its movement does to the competition.
Procurement Integrity.smes: Legal (JA) immediately; the HCA channel if the procurement is impacted.
Procurement Integrity.rule: RFO 3.104 protects two classes — source selection information and contractor bid/proposal data. Contain first, document everything; the written record closes the incident, not a reply email.

Organizational Conflict of Interest.qtype: an organizational-conflict-of-interest question — RFO 9.5: the type drives the remedy.
Organizational Conflict of Interest.smes: Legal (JA) and your reviewing chain; the HCA owns any waiver, non-delegable.
Organizational Conflict of Interest.rule: Identify the type first — unequal access, impaired objectivity, biased ground rules — then avoid, neutralize, or mitigate under RFO 9.5, in that order. A firewall can't fix ground rules already written.

Contractor Qualifications — Responsibili.qtype: a responsibility question — the seven RFO 9.104 standards, applied to today's facts.
Contractor Qualifications — Responsibili.smes: your contracting chain, Legal, and the SBA — a small-business referral is mandatory under RFO Part 19, and a CoC is conclusive.
Contractor Qualifications — Responsibili.rule: Doubt cuts in the Government's favor — doubt means no. But the 'no' must stand on the RFO 9.104 standards and documented facts, never on undocumented distrust.

Market Research.qtype: a market-research question — RFO Part 10: evidence before decisions.
Market Research.smes: the requiring activity's SMEs, your Small Business Professional, and industry itself — sources sought, RFIs, industry days.
Market Research.rule: RFO Part 10 research is the evidence; the commerciality, competition, and set-aside calls are decisions built on it. Undocumented research supports nothing downstream — and RFO 10.001 treats it as current for 18 months.

Required Sources of Supplies & Services.qtype: a required-sources question — the RFO Part 8 priority ladder before the open market.
Required Sources of Supplies & Services.smes: your policy shop, the AbilityOne/UNICOR program channels, and the schedule's ordering guide.
Required Sources of Supplies & Services.rule: Work the RFO Part 8 ladder in order — inventory, excess, UNICOR, AbilityOne, schedules — and mandatory means mandatory; price alone doesn't unlock the open market.

Commercial Products & Services.qtype: a commerciality question — the RFO 2.101 definition, the CID, and what RFO Part 12 changes.
Commercial Products & Services.smes: your pricing office, Legal, and the CID approval level one above you.
Commercial Products & Services.rule: Commercial rides the market: the RFO 2.101 definition (including minor mods that keep form, fit, and function) is a documented CID call over the SAT, and RFO Part 12 trades certified data for market evidence.

Simplified Acquisition Procedures.qtype: a simplified-acquisition question — RFO Part 13: the right lane by dollar band.
Simplified Acquisition Procedures.smes: your GPC program coordinator, Small Business Professional, and COCO.
Simplified Acquisition Procedures.rule: The band picks the RFO Part 13 lane: GPC to $15K, purchase orders to the $350K SAT — reserved for small business under the RFO Part 19 Rule of Two — and splitting a known requirement to stay under a threshold is a bright-line violation.

Small Business Programs.qtype: a small-business question — RFO Part 19: the Rule of Two and the program lanes.
Small Business Programs.smes: your Small Business Professional and the SBA PCR; DD Form 2579 documents the coordination.
Small Business Programs.rule: RFO Part 19: a reasonable expectation of two or more capable small businesses at fair market prices → set it aside. The rule tests the expectation at strategy time, not the final offer count.

Competition (CICA).qtype: a competition question — CICA and RFO Part 6: the default and the exception ladder.
Competition (CICA).smes: the Competition Advocate, Legal, and fresh market research to test the premise.
Competition (CICA).rule: Full and open is the default over the SAT (RFO 6.101). 'Other than' takes one of the seven RFO 6.103 exceptions in a J&A approved at the RFO 6.104 tier — and 'we've always used them' is not one of the seven.

Contracting by Negotiation — Source Sele.qtype: a source-selection question — RFO Part 15: fair process, documented judgment.
Contracting by Negotiation — Source Sele.smes: the SSA, your SSEB chairs, Legal, and the pricing office for the cost/price side.
Contracting by Negotiation — Source Sele.rule: The solicitation is the contract of the competition: evaluate exactly as Section M promised, keep RFO Part 15 exchanges in their lanes — clarifications, communications, discussions — and make discussions meaningful.

Certified Cost or Pricing Data & Proposa.qtype: a pricing question — RFO 15.403 on what data you're owed, RFO 15.404 on the analysis the file needs.
Certified Cost or Pricing Data & Proposa.smes: your pricing office, DCMA for field pricing and rates, DCAA for audit, and Legal on defective-pricing exposure.
Certified Cost or Pricing Data & Proposa.rule: Price analysis always (RFO 15.404-1). Certified data only past the threshold with the RFO 15.403-2 CLAWM exceptions checked first — and no award without a documented fair-and-reasonable determination.

Contract Types.qtype: a contract-type question — RFO Part 16: who carries the cost risk, and why.
Contract Types.smes: your pricing office, the PM on requirement certainty, and your reviewing chain for the D&F.
Contract Types.rule: RFO Part 16 matches risk to definition: FFP when the work prices firmly; cost-type (approved accounting system + D&F) when it can't. Forcing FFP onto the unknowable is risk denial, not risk transfer — and E.O. 14402 makes other-than-FFP a justified decision (RFO 16.104).

IDIQ Ordering & Fair Opportunity.qtype: a fair-opportunity question — RFO 16.507: every holder's real chance, or a documented exception.
IDIQ Ordering & Fair Opportunity.smes: the vehicle's PCO and ordering guide, the Competition Advocate for over-SAT D&As, and the ombudsman lane for holder complaints.
IDIQ Ordering & Fair Opportunity.rule: RFO 16.507-2 makes fair opportunity the default on multiple-award vehicles; exceptions (16.507-6) ride a D&A up the same approval ladder as J&As, and consideration must be genuine — not rotation paperwork.

Options.qtype: an options question — RFO Part 17: the exercise gates, applied to today.
Options.smes: FM for funds, the COR and PM on performance and continuing need, and Legal if the notice window slipped.
Options.rule: Exercise only through the RFO Part 17 gates: funds, continuing need, most-advantageous check, SAM exclusions, performance considered — with timely written notice, or the unilateral right lapses into a bilateral negotiation.

Interagency Acquisitions & the Economy A.qtype: an interagency question — RFO Part 17 interagency acquisition and the Economy Act (31 U.S.C. 1535): direct vs. assisted, and whose rules travel with the money.
Interagency Acquisitions & the Economy A.smes: FM (the fiscal rules travel with the funds), Legal, and the servicing agency's contracting office.
Interagency Acquisitions & the Economy A.rule: Pick the lane deliberately: direct (our CO orders on their vehicle) vs. assisted (their CO buys for us under a signed agreement). The Economy Act applies only absent a more specific authority — MIPR plus D&F.

Contract Finance & Fiscal Law.qtype: a fiscal-law question — Time, Purpose, Amount under the appropriations statutes, with RFO Part 32 carrying the financing side.
Contract Finance & Fiscal Law.smes: FM/Comptroller first and always, then Legal; the GAO Red Book and DoD FMR are the references.
Contract Finance & Fiscal Law.rule: Run T-P-A on every dollar: the right-year money for a bona fide need of that period, the appropriated purpose (31 U.S.C. 1301), within the available amount — Anti-Deficiency violations are the serious, reportable kind.
Contract Finance & Fiscal Law.cite: RFO Part 32 · GAO Red Book / DoD FMR · Vol. 2, Fiscal

Data Rights.qtype: a data-rights question — R-DFARS 227: the funding source drives the license.
Data Rights.smes: Legal (IP counsel), the program engineers on the component map, and DCMA on assertion administration.
Data Rights.rule: R-DFARS 227: who paid for development answers most of it — Government funds → unlimited, mixed → GPR, private → limited/restricted. The contractor proves the restriction (the 252.227-7017 assertion list); honor the markings until a challenge resolves.

Contract Modifications & Scope.qtype: a scope question — RFO Part 43: a modification, or a new procurement in disguise.
Contract Modifications & Scope.smes: Legal, the PCO chain, and the original competition record itself.
Contract Modifications & Scope.rule: The test is what the original competitors reasonably anticipated — judged against the original contract with all mods cumulative. In scope: modify under RFO Part 43. Beyond it: compete it or justify it under RFO Part 6.

Government Property.qtype: a Government-property question — RFO Part 45: the default rule and the four-part exception.
Government Property.smes: the property administrator, DCMA, and the PM — who owes the written justification.
Government Property.rule: RFO Part 45: contractors furnish property. GFP only when all four parts hold — best interest, benefit over burden, no substantial risk shift, not otherwise satisfiable — and furnishing it puts the Government's own performance on the schedule.

Undefinitized Contract Actions.qtype: a UCA question — R-DFARS 217.74: undefinitized work and decaying negotiation leverage.
Undefinitized Contract Actions.smes: your pricing office, the clearance authority, and Legal; DCMA for actuals once performance starts.
Undefinitized Contract Actions.rule: R-DFARS 217.74 makes UCAs the exception: 50% obligation cap (75% after the qualifying proposal), definitize within 180 days, clearance at definitization — and neither poor planning nor administrative convenience ever justifies one.

Clearance — Independent Review & Approva.qtype: a clearance question — DAF clearance procedures: independent review before the Government commits.
Clearance — Independent Review & Approva.smes: the clearance authority itself, your chief, and Legal on any compliance flags.
Clearance — Independent Review & Approva.rule: Two gates catching two failures: business clearance blesses the strategy before release; contract clearance blesses the negotiated result before award. The selector never approves the selection.

Protests.qtype: a protest question — RFO Part 33 and CICA: venue, stay math, and the record you built months earlier.
Protests.smes: Legal drives; GAO or COFC counsel through Legal; the HCA owns any override decision.
Protests.rule: Know the RFO 33.105 machinery cold — the 10-day/5-day stay rule, three venues with different powers — and remember the real defense was built earlier: criteria stated, followed, and documented.

REAs & Claims.qtype: a disputes question — the Contract Disputes Act and RFO Part 33: REA lane or CDA claim, and substance beats the label.
REAs & Claims.smes: Legal early, FM on funding the outcome, and the COR/PM for the facts record.
REAs & Claims.rule: Classify by substance under the CDA: a sum certain, certified, with a decision demanded is a claim — interest and decision deadlines already running. The machinery doesn't care what the cover letter says.
REAs & Claims.cite: Contract Disputes Act · RFO Part 33 · Vol. 2, REAs & Claims

Terminations.qtype: a termination question — RFO Part 49 (or the commercial clause under RFO 12.403): fault drives the remedy.
Terminations.smes: Legal (mandatory), your termination contracting officer channel, and DCMA on settlement.
Terminations.rule: Who's at fault decides what's owed under RFO Part 49: T4C makes the contractor whole for work done, no anticipatory profit; T4D demands the full runway — cure, show cause, excusability — because a wrongful default converts to a T4C.

R&D Contracting — BAAs, SBIR & OTs.qtype: an R&D-authorities question — RFO Part 35, the SBIR statute, and 10 U.S.C. 4022 OTs: the right instrument for genuine uncertainty.
R&D Contracting — BAAs, SBIR & OTs.smes: your agreements officer channel, Legal, and the S&T program office.
R&D Contracting — BAAs, SBIR & OTs.rule: Pick the authority for a reason: RFO Part 35 BAAs compete proposals against a published standard, SBIR Phase III carries statutory sole-source off competed early phases, and 10 U.S.C. 4022 OTs trade the mature protections framework for agility — 'skipping the rules' is never the reason.
R&D Contracting — BAAs, SBIR & OTs.cite: RFO Part 35 · SBIR statute · 10 U.S.C. 4022 · Vol. 2, R&D

Construction & Service Contracting.qtype: a construction/services question — RFO Parts 36 and 37, with RFO Part 28 bonds: specialized statutory machinery.
Construction & Service Contracting.smes: Legal, the labor advisor on wage determinations, and the installation civil engineers.
Construction & Service Contracting.rule: Construction and services run on their own rails: RFO Part 28 bonds over $150K, written notice before disturbing a differing site condition (RFO Part 36), qualifications-based A&E selection, and no personal-services drift (RFO Part 37).
Construction & Service Contracting.cite: RFO Parts 36/37 · Part 28 bonds · Vol. 2, Construction

Openers & Perspective.qtype: a perspective question — the panel is testing how you think as a business leader, not what you can recite.
Openers & Perspective.smes: Nobody to phone — this one is yours. Anchor on your own experience, your office, and what you actually control.
Openers & Perspective.rule: Answer in your own voice with a definition, a concrete plan, and one example — and show the judgment to know where the boring answer is the right one.
Openers & Perspective.cite: Your own experience — verify anything you cite at acquisition.gov/far-overhaul

_generic.qtype: a frameworks question — name it, then walk it.
_generic.smes: your CO/chief, Legal (JA), and FM — the standing phone-a-friends.
_generic.rule: State the default rule first, then the exception you'd need, then the facts that earn it — in that order, out loud.
